# Grouping and choosing among equal INTERVAL values
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#interval_type
#
# INTERVAL values compare by their length, with 30 days to a month and 24 hours to a day, so
# INTERVAL 1 MONTH and INTERVAL 30 DAY are equal but print differently. GoogleSQL's compliance
# tests group them together but normalize the value they return before comparing it. These ask
# which of the equal values BigQuery returns, and whether that depends on the input's order: each
# question is asked with the values in both orders.

# GROUP BY and DISTINCT: how many groups, and which value each returns.

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT i FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY]) AS i GROUP BY i
)
?>

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT i FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 MONTH]) AS i GROUP BY i
)
?>

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT i FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 720 HOUR, INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 MONTH]) AS i GROUP BY i
)
?>

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT i FROM UNNEST([MAKE_INTERVAL(month => 1, day => -1), INTERVAL 29 DAY]) AS i GROUP BY i
)
?>

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT i FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY]) AS i
)
?>

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT i FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 MONTH]) AS i
)
?>

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i)
FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY, MAKE_INTERVAL(month => 2, day => -30)]) AS i
?>

# Set operations.

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT INTERVAL 1 MONTH AS i UNION DISTINCT SELECT INTERVAL 30 DAY
)
?>

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT INTERVAL 30 DAY AS i UNION DISTINCT SELECT INTERVAL 1 MONTH
)
?>

SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(i AS STRING)) FROM (
  SELECT INTERVAL 1 MONTH AS i INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT INTERVAL 30 DAY
)
?>

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT INTERVAL 1 MONTH AS i EXCEPT DISTINCT SELECT INTERVAL 720 HOUR
)
?>

# PARTITION BY puts equal values in one partition.

SELECT ARRAY(
  SELECT COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY i)
  FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 DAY]) AS i
  ORDER BY 1
)
?>

# MIN and MAX between equal values.

SELECT CAST(MAX(i) AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY]) AS i
?>

SELECT CAST(MAX(i) AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 MONTH]) AS i
?>

SELECT CAST(MIN(i) AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY]) AS i
?>

SELECT CAST(MIN(i) AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 MONTH]) AS i
?>

SELECT ARRAY(
  SELECT CAST(MAX(i) OVER (ORDER BY k) AS STRING)
  FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS k, INTERVAL 1 MONTH AS i), (2, INTERVAL 30 DAY), (3, INTERVAL 1 DAY)])
  ORDER BY k
)
?>

# SUM and AVG with DISTINCT: which of the equal values they add.

SELECT CAST(SUM(DISTINCT i) AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY]) AS i
?>

SELECT CAST(SUM(DISTINCT i) AS STRING) FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 MONTH]) AS i
?>

SELECT CAST(AVG(DISTINCT i) AS STRING)
FROM UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 2 DAY]) AS i
?>

# GREATEST, LEAST and NULLIF between equal values.

SELECT CAST(GREATEST(INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY) AS STRING)
?>

SELECT CAST(GREATEST(INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS STRING)
?>

SELECT CAST(LEAST(INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY) AS STRING)
?>

SELECT CAST(LEAST(INTERVAL 30 DAY, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS STRING)
?>

SELECT CAST(NULLIF(INTERVAL 1 MONTH, INTERVAL 30 DAY) AS STRING)
?>
